summary: The bad() method opens a FileReader wrapped in a BufferedReader but never releases them, leaking the file descriptor/handle (CWE-775) on both the success and exception paths. I added a finally block that closes the BufferedReader and FileReader (guarded for null and wrapped in their own try/catch so a close failure is logged rather than masking the read), ensuring the descriptor is always released while preserving the read-and-print behavior for valid input.
